result:
The partner reverted one ruling and answered the night-email question. Here is what I would do, in order: implement the revert now as a follow-up task, then run the rest of the plan-completion protocol, then delete the workspace.

**1. Record the partner's answers in the ledger**

<edit path=".sdd/12-dock-alerts/progress.md">
Gate: Partner reverted Task 3 Ruling (module name): module goes back to `alerts/send.py` as the plan wrote it. Follow-up Task 5 implements this now.
Gate: Partner kept Task 2 threshold ruling, Task 3 one-email-per-alert ruling, and Final retry-jitter ruling.
Gate: Declined to judge "email for alerts at night": partner ruled email is fine. No change, no deferred item.
</edit>

**2. Follow-up Task 5: rename back to `alerts/send.py`**

First I would find every reference so the brief has the full list:

<command>
git grep -nE "alerts\.notify|alerts import notify|from \.notify|import notify" -- ':!specs' ':!.sdd'
</command>

Then I would dispatch one implementer subagent with this brief:
- Run `git mv alerts/notify.py alerts/send.py`.
- Update every import found above, including tests.
- Watch for the hazard behind the original ruling. The service already imports a socket helper named `send`, so no module may bind a bare name `send` to both. Where the two meet, import the alert function as `from alerts.send import send_alert` and never `from alerts import send`.
- Run the full test suite and commit the change as one commit.

After that I would dispatch the code-reviewer on that commit only. I would focus it on name shadowing and on any import of `alerts.notify` that was missed. When the review is clean, I would add this line to the ledger:

<edit path=".sdd/12-dock-alerts/progress.md">
Task 5 (gate follow-up): complete (commits 0b1c2d3..<new-sha>, review clean)
</edit>

**3. Record the ruling that contradicts the spec in `specs/history.md`**

This entry takes the place of a spec amendment.

<edit path="specs/history.md">
## Plan 12: dock alerts (specs/plans/12-dock-alerts.md), completed 2026-11-18
- Ruling (contradicts spec: § 2 Alert threshold): docks alert at 3 or fewer free slots, not 2 or fewer. Docks refill more slowly than the design assumed, so 2 free slots leaves riders no warning. Cost if wrong: about one extra alert a day.
- Kept as written: § 3 Alert channel. Email, one email per alert, confirmed for night-time alerts too.
</edit>

**4. Mark up the plan**

<edit path="specs/plans/12-dock-alerts.md">
Status: complete (2026-11-18). Tasks 1–4 done, plus follow-up Task 5 (module name reverted to `alerts/send.py` at the completion gate). See specs/history.md for the § 2 threshold ruling.
</edit>

**5. Deferred items:** none. The only reverted ruling was implemented now, no review findings are unfixed, and the night-email question is resolved. `specs/deferred_items.md` is left unchanged.

**6. Retire the plan, then delete the workspace**

<command>
git mv specs/plans/12-dock-alerts.md specs/plans/completed/12-dock-alerts.md && git commit -am "Complete plan 12: dock alerts"
</command>

<command>
rm -rf .sdd/12-dock-alerts
</command>

---

**Message to partner:**

> Done.
> - **Module name:** `alerts/notify.py` is back to `alerts/send.py`, with all imports updated (commit `<new-sha>`). The suite passes and the review was clean. One note: the original rename was there because a bare `send` name collides with the socket helper. The fix imports `send_alert` directly to avoid that collision, so nothing shadows anything now.
> - **Threshold (3 or fewer free slots):** this stands. It is recorded in `specs/history.md` as a departure from spec § 2.
> - **One email per alert, retry-jitter:** both stand as decided.
> - **Night-time alerts:** they stay on email, so nothing changed.
>
> No deferred items. The plan is in `specs/plans/completed/` and its workspace is deleted. The branch `feat/dock-alerts` is ready to finish.
